title: Product Photo Lighting Without a Studio | AIVideosUGC
description: Product photo lighting for glass, metal, and gloss. Fix a harsh snapshot with soft, directional light and clean highlights, from one uploaded photo.
h1: Product Photo Lighting for Glass, Metal and Gloss
lead: Upload one clear photo and describe the light so glass, metal, and gloss stay easy to see, without a studio kit.
secondary_keywords: skincare product photo with soft light

steps.d: Upload a sharp photo of the whole product, with the edges that catch light in focus. A plain snapshot is enough.
Name the light direction, how soft the shadow should be, and how glass or metal should look. The result is a square photo.
Download the image and compare its silhouette, color and finish with the real item. Add any offer text in your editor after export.

faq.q: Which products show a useful lighting change?
faq.a: Glass, metal, ceramic, and glossy items can show a useful change in highlight and shadow. Compare the download with the real surface before you publish.

faq.q: Do I need a studio setup?
faq.a: No. A clear phone photo can become a softly lit product image. The job uses credits instead of a lighting kit.

faq.q: Can I reduce glare on glass or metal?
faq.a: The generated image can soften highlights and keep the product face easier to read. Reflective results still need a review, because a highlight can shift.

faq.q: Will the new lighting change the shape or color?
faq.a: It can. Compare the silhouette, color, and finish with the real item whenever those must stay exact.

faq.q: Which light suits an Amazon listing?
faq.a: Use even light from the front when shoppers need a clear product face. Save stronger contrast for ads and detail views.

faq.q: Can I describe a light direction?
faq.a: Yes. Describe the direction, the shadow softness and the surface you want to read, then compare the result with the real item.

faq.q: What does a lighting photo cost?
faq.a: Each product photo costs 24 credits. The cost is shown before the job starts, and a failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Does the lighting photo have a watermark?
faq.a: No. You can use it in a listing or your own ad. Compare glass, metal, and gloss with the real item first.

faq.q: Can I use one relit photo in both a listing and an ad?
faq.a: Yes. Use the even, front-lit version as the listing face, and keep a higher-contrast version for the ad.

faq.q: Can I add offer text on the photo?
faq.a: Add the offer in your editor after export. The lighting photo does not add prices or other words.

steps.prompt: Give this white mug warm window light from the side, a soft shadow, and a clear highlight on the glaze. Keep the rim, handle, and color as they are.
steps.sourceHint: Show the full mug, rim and handle in focus.

items.d: A fragrance shop uses soft side light on a perfume bottle so the glass edge stays easy to see.
A skincare shop uses even front light on a cream jar for the listing, instead of a hard highlight.
A watch shop puts a narrow highlight on the case rim and checks that the shape did not shift.
A drinkware shop keeps the reflection on a steel cup controlled, instead of a bright glare.
A jewelry shop runs light along a chain so the metal is easy to see, without a lighting kit.
A ceramic shop puts a glossy cup on a plain surface with a soft shadow.
An audio shop pulls the glare off a speaker panel so the controls stay visible.
A candle shop uses a gentle rim light on a glass jar for an ad, not for the main listing face.
A makeup shop puts a small highlight on a compact lid and compares it with the real finish before posting.
A bottle shop uses even front light on clear glass so the label area is easier to see.
